article_title: Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses
news_headline: Tech Rout Erases Record $2.3 Trillion in Value as AI Fears Grow
post_text:
On November 5, the Nasdaq 100 dropped 6.4% in a single session, wiping out $2.3 trillion in market value, its worst day since the onset of Covid in March 2020. The trigger was a combination of investor anxiety over whether AI infrastructure spending will ever generate commensurate returns, and fears that the Democratic midterm sweep would bring tighter AI regulation. Semiconductor stocks bore the worst of it, with a gauge of US chipmakers falling 12% in one day.

The selloff is a stress test of a thesis that markets had priced in with little skepticism: that the AI buildout justifies the extraordinary multiples attached to it. For months, capital rotated almost reflexively into anything AI-adjacent, leaving little room for the possibility that the ROI takes longer, costs more, or gets politically complicated.

WBR's piece 'Beyond AI Multiples: The Value in Boring Businesses' made exactly this argument, that the sprint toward AI at ~30x revenue multiples crowds out the unglamorous, cash-generative businesses that don't make headlines but do make money. This week's rout didn't disprove AI's long-term potential, but it did confirm that chasing multiples without scrutinizing fundamentals has a price. The full piece is on the WBR website.
